input.content:
## Why

PR builds push a `pr-<N>` handoff tag for **both** Linux images:
`build.yml`'s matrix covers `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` (`:48-55`), and
the GHCR ref is built from `matrix.name` (`:64`, `:132-138`). Cleanup deletes
one of them. `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26` hardcodes
`PACKAGE_NAME: flutter-android`, and that single name is what the two API calls
query (`:66`, `:82`).

So every closed PR leaves a `flutter-web:pr-<N>` tag behind. Counted against
GHCR on 2026-08-10:

| Package | Handoff tags present |
|---|---|
| `flutter-android` | 2 — both open PRs, expected |
| `flutter-web` | **22** — `pr-513` through `pr-543` |

Each orphan is a full image index carrying SBOM and provenance attestations
(`build.yml:151-155`), not a bare tag. The count grows by one per PR.

The spec has the same defect: `ci-image-tag-lifecycle`'s Purpose and both
deletion requirements are scoped to `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android`
(`spec.md:5,11,17,43`). The workflow matches its spec — the spec was written
when `flutter-android` was the only image and never revisited when
`flutter-web` was added.

Relevance gate: this changes what a maintainer finds when auditing GHCR
storage — one tag per open PR, as the capability already promises, rather than
one per ever-opened PR on an image nobody was cleaning.

## What Changes

- `cleanup-pr-image.yml` iterates the images that produce handoff tags instead
  of naming one, with `fail-fast: false` so one image's failure does not skip
  another's.
- The 22 existing `flutter-web` orphans are swept once. The workflow fires only
  on `pull_request: closed` and `delete`, so it will never revisit tags for
  PRs that are already closed.
- `ci-image-tag-lifecycle` is de-scoped from `flutter-android` — its Purpose
  and its two deletion requirements.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Declaring the published image set in a config file. The image list here is
  short, local, and about which images produce *handoff tags* — a narrower
  question than which images are published. If a declaration lands later this
  workflow is a natural consumer, but it is not a prerequisite.
- `flutter-windows`, which produces no handoff tags: `windows.yml` calls
  `windows-image.yml` with `push: false` (`windows.yml:19-22`), so a PR
  builds it without pushing anything to delete.
- The two image-agnostic requirements in the capability, *Cleanup never
  targets a non-handoff tag* (`spec.md:47`) and *Cleanup workflow runs with
  minimum privilege* (`:68`). Both already hold for any image.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `ci-image-tag-lifecycle`: its two deletion requirements are de-scoped from
  `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android` to every image that produces handoff tags,
  and gain the guarantee that one image's cleanup failure does not skip
  another's.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/cleanup-pr-image.yml` (matrix over the image
names, `fail-fast: false`); `openspec/specs/ci-image-tag-lifecycle/spec.md` on
archive, including its Purpose line (`:5`).

**One-off**: sweep the orphaned `flutter-web` handoff tags. Deletion must
resolve a specific `pr-<N>` tag to a version ID and delete by ID — a
`tags == []` filter would match OCI index children and break parent tags.

**Verification**: after the sweep, each package should carry handoff tags only
for open PRs. The next closed PR should leave neither image with a `pr-<N>`
tag.

**Risk**: the sweep is a destructive registry operation. It is bounded by the
existing tag-regex guard (`:49-52`), which refuses anything that is not
`pr-<N>` or `branch-<ref>`, keeping release tags and `buildcache` unreachable —
but the one-off sweep runs outside that workflow, so it needs the same guard
applied deliberately rather than inherited.

### Requirement: Windows release uses the same metadata conventions as Android release

The Windows release build SHALL use `docker/metadata-action` with the `images` input set to the same three registry namespaces and the `tags` input set to `type=raw,value=${{ env.FLUTTER_VERSION }}`, mirroring the Android job. This metadata step runs inside the reusable `windows-image.yml` workflow invoked by the `release-windows` caller. The image labels (`org.opencontainers.image.*`) produced by `metadata-action` SHALL be applied to the built image (as `--label` arguments to `docker build`), so that `docker inspect` reports the same OCI label set as the Android image. `docker/build-push-action` is not a viable mechanism here because it does not support Windows containers (tracked at https://github.com/docker/build-push-action/issues/18).

The experience context is the operator inspecting `docker inspect <org>/flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` and `docker inspect <org>/flutter-android:X.Y.Z` and finding the same set of OCI labels (description, source, revision, version) populated with the same values.

#### Scenario: Labels match Android conventions

- **GIVEN** a successful `release-windows` run for tag `X.Y.Z`
- **WHEN** an operator runs `docker inspect docker.io/<org>/flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` and inspects the `Labels` map
- **THEN** the keys `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `org.opencontainers.image.revision`, `org.opencontainers.image.version`, and `org.opencontainers.image.title` are all present
- **AND** `org.opencontainers.image.version` equals `X.Y.Z`
- **AND** `org.opencontainers.image.revision` equals the commit SHA of the tag

input.content:
## Why

`flutter-windows`'s Docker Hub page is never synced from `readme.md`. The
`update-description` job's matrix (`release.yml:184-186`) lists
`flutter-android` and `flutter-web` only, so a CI engineer landing on the
Windows image's Docker Hub page finds whatever is there by default, while the
other two images carry the project readme.

This is the same matrix omission that kept `flutter-windows` out of Docker
Scout ([#506]) — but where the Scout exclusion turns out to be correct on
technical grounds, this one is simply a gap. `peter-evans/dockerhub-description`
is an API call against a repository name; it has no Linux dependency and no
reason to skip a Windows image.

The spec layer has the same gap, and its shape shows where the fix belongs.
Description sync is specified **per image, in that image's own release
capability**: `web-image-release/spec.md:57` says "The Docker Hub repository
description for `flutter-web` SHALL be synced from `readme.md` on release, as
the Android image is." `windows-image-release`'s parallel requirement,
*Windows release uses the same metadata conventions as Android release*
(`spec.md:49`), covers registry namespaces, tags, and OCI labels — and stops
short of the description sentence its web counterpart carries.

Relevance gate: this changes what a CI engineer sees when they open
`hub.docker.com/r/<org>/flutter-windows` — the same project readme the other
two images show, rather than an empty page for the one image published by a
different job.

## What Changes

- `update-description` covers `flutter-windows`.
- `windows-image-release`'s metadata-conventions requirement gains the
  description-sync sentence, matching how `web-image-release` states the same
  thing for `flutter-web`.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Declaring the published image set in a config file. Description sync is
  specified per image in each image's release capability, so the fix is one
  sentence in the capability that already owns the Windows image's metadata
  conventions. A declaration would be a different change with a different
  argument.
- `record-image`. Its omission of `flutter-windows` is correct and is handled
  by the `windows-scout-scope` change.
- `verify-published`, which already covers all three images
  (`release.yml:149-153`).

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `windows-image-release`: its metadata-conventions requirement gains Docker
  Hub description sync, so the Windows image's registry presentation matches
  the Android and web images rather than stopping at OCI labels.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (`update-description`'s matrix,
`:184-186`); `openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md:49` on archive.

**Prerequisite to verify before implementing**: the `flutter-windows`
repository must exist on Docker Hub. `peter-evans/dockerhub-description` fails
if it does not. The release path pushes there (`windows-image.yml:92-94`), so
it should exist — but this is unconfirmed, and an unconfirmed assumption here
surfaces as a failed release job.

**Verification**: after the next release, `hub.docker.com/r/<org>/flutter-windows`
shows the project readme, and the `update-description` run shows three legs.

**Risk**: low, with one asymmetry worth noting. `update-description` declares
`needs: release-linux` (`release.yml:178`) — a Linux job — while the image it
would now describe is published by `release-windows`. This change adds the
matrix leg without restructuring that dependency, so on a Windows-only
`workflow_dispatch` the job is skipped by its own event guard (`:181`) and no
description is synced. That is existing behaviour for every image and is not
made worse here; a change that reworks post-publish dependencies would revisit
it.

[#506]: https://github.com/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/issues/506

### Review result: APPROVED_WITH_WARNINGS

### CRITICAL issues

None. Every file:line citation in the artifacts checks out against `05b2919`, and the load-bearing GitHub Actions claim is correct.

Verification record for the items I was asked to scrutinize:

- **`release.yml:22`** is `  release-linux:` — the proposal's claim that "no job named `release-android` exists (the code says `release-linux`)" is **correct**.
- **`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284`** each read exactly `if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled() }}` — **correct**, and all three are the `update-description` / `record-image` / `create-github-release` guards as claimed.
- **`release.yml:235-237`** is `matrix:` / `include:` / `- name: flutter-android` — the matrix block, **correct** as an anchor (the two legs are `:237-238`; the cited range points at the block head, which is fine for "add a comment here").
- **`release.yml:137-141`** is the `verify-published` comment plus its `needs:` line — a genuine precedent for "a comment recording why a job is wired the way it is." **Correct**.
- **`windows.Dockerfile:3`** is the `servercore:ltsc2025@sha256:...` pinned `FROM`. **Correct**. `:20` (Git from zip), `:42` (Flutter via `git clone`), `:74` (VS Build Tools installer) all match.
- **`windows-image-release/spec.md:65`** says downstream jobs "SHALL be skipped via an `if: github.event_name == 'push'` guard on `release-android` (the downstream jobs auto-skip via their existing `needs: release-android`)". The proposal's characterization is **correct and the spec is wrong twice over** — no `release-android` job exists, and no downstream job relies on a `needs:`-propagated skip.

**Scrutiny item 1 — the `!cancelled()` semantics claim is correct.** GitHub's skip-propagation rule is "If a job fails or is skipped, all jobs that need it are skipped *unless the jobs use a conditional expression that causes the job to continue*." The propagation is not a separate hard-coded rule — it is the implicit default `success()` status check doing the work, and per the expressions reference, "A default status check of `success()` is applied unless you include one of these functions." `!cancelled()` contains the status-check function `cancelled()`, which suppresses the implicit `success()`; `cancelled()` keys off *workflow* cancellation, not ancestor conclusions, so with `release-linux` skipped and no cancellation it evaluates false and `!cancelled()` is true. The dependents run on the strength of their own guard alone. Sources: [workflow-syntax `jobs.<job_id>.needs`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idneeds), [expressions — status check functions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions#status-check-functions). The MODIFIED requirement's sentence — "A dependent job that declares `if: ... && !cancelled()` does not auto-skip when its dependency is skipped" — is accurate.

**Scrutiny item 3 — the MODIFIED requirement restates the original faithfully.** Diffing `spec.md:63-84` against the delta: it correctly renames `release-android` → "the Linux release job", preserves the `workflow_dispatch:` declaration, the `FLUTTER_VERSION` from `github.ref_name`, the three post-publish jobs, the experience context, and both scenarios. Two additions are deliberate and disclosed (the new mechanism paragraph; the new `AND` at delta `:50`). The `flutter-android` digest scenario is retained verbatim. No behavior is silently dropped.

**Scrutiny item 5 — no unmarked contradiction with a main spec.** I grepped all 24 main specs for Scout/scan/record and for `flutter-windows`. No main spec asserts `flutter-windows` is scanned or recorded. `ci-image-vulnerability-scan` is scoped entirely to the PR-time `scan_image` job on `flutter-android` and needs no delta, exactly as task 3.2 predicts. `ci-image-anonymous-availability` independently guarantees Windows anonymous-pull verification, which is what the ADDED requirement's second scenario leans on — consistent, no delta needed.

### Warnings

**1. The ADDED requirement mandates a code comment — implementation, not observable behavior.** `changes/windows-scout-scope/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md:5`:

> "The exclusion SHALL be recorded where `record-image`'s legs are listed, so a reader who notices the omission finds the decision at the point of omission."

and its scenario at `:17`: "**THEN** the exclusion and its reason are recorded where the legs are listed".

`config.yaml` marks as CRITICAL: *"Reject if spec describes implementation without connection to what the desktop user would notice"*. This does not quite trip that gate — the requirement carries an explicit experience context at `:11` (the maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` absent from the code-scanning dashboard), so the connection is stated rather than absent. But the requirement pins the *location* of a YAML comment, which is a source-layout fact, not a behavior. The durable requirement is "`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, justified by Scout's analysis support"; *where* the note lives belongs in `tasks.md` (where 1.1-1.3 already say it, in more detail). Recommend softening `:5`'s second sentence and the `:17` scenario to be about the decision being recorded and discoverable, leaving the anchor point to the tasks.

`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, and the exclusion SHALL be justified by Scout's analysis support rather than by which job builds the image. The exclusion and its justification SHALL be discoverable by a maintainer reading the job that records images in Scout.

Three independent facts each make the analysis impossible, and all three SHALL be recorded with enough detail to be re-derived:

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images only; the published image is `windows/amd64` | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/>; image platform from the registry config blob for the published tag |
| Scout's analysis size limit is 4 GB compressed; the published image is 5.90 GB | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/>; size from summing layer sizes in the published tag's manifest |
| Scout carries no Microsoft advisory feed, and the image installs Git, the Flutter SDK, and VS Build Tools outside any package manager, so no SBOM-driven scanner finds an inventory to match | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/>; install mechanisms visible in `windows.Dockerfile` |

The exclusion SHALL hold only while those facts hold. If Docker Scout adds Windows image support, raises the size limit above the published image's size, or adds a Microsoft advisory feed, this requirement SHALL be revisited rather than carried forward unexamined.

The record SHALL name what governs the Windows image's CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image digest pinned in `windows.Dockerfile`, and the cadence at which that pin is bumped.

No dependency on the sibling changes, but two coordination notes: this change
and `windows-description-sync` both edit `release.yml` (different matrices —

`openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md` on archive (different

`pr-tag-cleanup-all-images` is disjoint from both.

## 1. Record the exclusion where it is noticed

- [ ] 1.1 Add a comment at `record-image`'s matrix (`release.yml:235-237`) stating that `flutter-windows` is excluded, with all three reasons and the source for each: Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only while the image is `windows/amd64`; the 4 GB compressed limit against the image's 5.90 GB; and no Microsoft advisory feed, with the image's tools installed outside any package manager
- [ ] 1.2 Include the two `docs.docker.com` URLs the requirement cites, so the comment is re-verifiable without the proposal
- [ ] 1.3 Name the control that does apply — the `servercore` digest pin at `windows.Dockerfile:3` and its bump cadence — so the comment points somewhere rather than only saying "no"
- [ ] 1.4 Keep the comment's shape consistent with the neighbouring one at `release.yml:137-141`, the repo's existing precedent for recording why a job is wired the way it is

## 2. Correct the spec that misdescribes the skip

- [ ] 2.1 On archive, replace `windows-image-release/spec.md:65`'s `needs: release-android` justification with the event-guard mechanism the code actually uses: `update-description` (`release.yml:181`), `record-image` (`:232`), and `create-github-release` (`:284`) each carry `if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled() }}`, and `!cancelled()` suppresses the implicit `success()` status check that would otherwise propagate a skip from a `needs:` dependency
- [ ] 2.2 Stop naming `release-android` — the job is `release-linux` (`release.yml:22`) and has been since `flutter-web` was added
- [ ] 2.3 Apply the same `release-android` → Linux release job correction to the requirement's scenarios (`spec.md:81-82`)

- [ ] 3.1 Confirm the `release.yml` diff touches only comment lines inside the `record-image` block — no matrix entry, `if:`, `needs:`, or step is modified. This change alters no behaviour, and the diff is the check

- [ ] 3.3 Re-check the three disqualifiers against Docker's current docs before merging — they are the whole basis of the requirement, and the requirement makes the exclusion conditional on them
- [ ] 3.4 After the next release, confirm `record-image` ran with the same two legs and the same SARIF categories as before. This resolves only on a tag push, so it is a post-merge observation, not a merge gate

- [ ] 4.1 Close [#506] citing the three disqualifiers, so the exclusion is recorded on the issue as a decision rather than a deferral

toolUseResult.originalFile:
## Why

`flutter-windows` has never been analyzed by Docker Scout. The `record-image`
job's matrix (`release.yml:235-237`) lists `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`
only, so no Scout environment record or CVE SARIF is produced for the Windows
image and it is absent from the code-scanning dashboard ([#506]).

[#506] asks to verify whether Scout produces meaningful output for a Windows
image before wiring it up. It does not, on three independent grounds — each
one disqualifying on its own:

1. **Architecture.** Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only
   ([docs](https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/)). The published image
   is `os: windows, arch: amd64`, read from its registry config blob rather
   than inferred. Not fixable: Windows containers are `windows/amd64` by
   construction.
2. **Size.** The same limit is 4 GB compressed. The published image is
   **5.90 GB across 37 layers**, the `servercore` base alone being 1.42 GB.
3. **No advisory data, and no inventory to apply it to.** Scout's 23 advisory
   sources include no Microsoft/MSRC feed, and every OS ecosystem it supports
   is a Linux one
   ([sources](https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/)).
   Nor would another scanner help: `windows.Dockerfile` installs Git from a zip
   (`:20`), Flutter via `git clone` (`:42`), and VS Build Tools via an
   installer (`:74`). None is registered with a package manager, so an
   SBOM-driven scanner finds an empty inventory. Trivy's supported-OS table has
   no Windows row; Grype delegates cataloguing to Syft, which has no MSI or KB
   cataloger.

So the current behaviour is right and the omission is not a bug. What is wrong
is that nothing says so: the exclusion reads as an oversight, and the spec that
does mention it justifies it by the wrong thing (see below).

Relevance gate: this changes what a maintainer finds when they notice
`flutter-windows` missing from the code-scanning dashboard — a recorded
decision and a pointer to what does govern its CVE posture, instead of a gap
that invites the same investigation again.

## What Changes

- A new requirement in `windows-image-release` stating that `flutter-windows`
  is out of scope for Docker Scout, carrying all three disqualifiers, and
  naming what governs its CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image
  digest pin (`windows.Dockerfile:3`) and how promptly it is bumped. Microsoft
  rebuilds Windows base images monthly on Patch Tuesday.
- The existing *Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only* requirement
  is corrected. It currently justifies `record-image` skipping via
  `needs: release-android` (`spec.md:65`) — wrong twice over: no job named
  `release-android` exists (the code says `release-linux`, `release.yml:22`),
  and the skip is not produced by a `needs:` edge at all. Each downstream job
  carries an explicit `if: github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled()` guard
  (`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284`), and under `!cancelled()` a skipped
  dependency does **not** auto-skip its dependents. The spec describes a
  mechanism the code does not use.
- A comment at `record-image`'s matrix recording the exclusion and its reason,
  so the omission is legible where someone would notice it.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Adding a Windows-capable scanner. Researched and rejected above.
- Any change to which images `record-image` actually records. Behaviour is
  unchanged; only its justification and legibility change.
- Declaring the published image set in a config file. That is a separate
  concern with its own defects to fix, and coupling it here is what made an
  earlier attempt at this change unreviewable.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `windows-image-release`: gains a requirement placing `flutter-windows` out of
  scope for Docker Scout on stated technical grounds; its
  `workflow_dispatch` requirement is corrected to describe the skip mechanism
  the code actually uses and to stop naming a job that does not exist.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a comment at `record-image`'s
matrix, `:235-237`); `openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md` on archive.

**No behaviour change.** `record-image`'s legs are identical before and after.
This change makes a decision legible and corrects a spec that misdescribes the
code; it does not alter what runs.

**Verification**: `record-image` runs on the next release with the same two
legs and the same SARIF categories. The spec correction is checked by reading
`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284` — the `if:` guards that actually produce the
dispatch skip.

**Risk**: low. The one judgement call is that the three disqualifiers are
durable. Architecture is structural; size has headroom in the wrong direction
(5.90 GB against 4 GB, and the image grows); the advisory-feed gap is
Docker's to close and would be announced. If Scout ever adds Windows support
the requirement should be revisited, not silently kept.

[#506]: https://github.com/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/issues/506

8	[#506] asks to verify whether Scout produces meaningful output for a Windows
9	image before wiring it up. It does not, on three independent grounds — each
10	one disqualifying on its own:
11	
12	1. **Architecture.** Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only

18	   **5.90 GB across 37 layers**, the `servercore` base alone being 1.42 GB.

26	   SBOM-driven scanner finds an empty inventory. Trivy's supported-OS table has
27	   no Windows row; Grype delegates cataloguing to Syft, which has no MSI or KB
28	   cataloger.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The Windows image is out of scope for Docker Scout

`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, and the exclusion SHALL be justified by Scout's analysis support rather than by which job builds the image. The exclusion and its justification SHALL be discoverable by a maintainer reading the job that records images in Scout.

Three independent facts each make the analysis impossible, and all three SHALL be recorded with enough detail to be re-derived:

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images only; the published image is `windows/amd64` | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/>; image platform from the registry config blob for the published tag |
| Scout's analysis size limit is 4 GB compressed; the published image is 5.90 GB | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/>; size from summing layer sizes in the published tag's manifest |
| Scout carries no Microsoft advisory feed, and the image installs Git, the Flutter SDK, and VS Build Tools outside any package manager, so no SBOM-driven scanner finds an inventory to match | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/>; install mechanisms visible in `windows.Dockerfile` |

The exclusion SHALL hold only while those facts hold. If Docker Scout adds Windows image support, raises the size limit above the published image's size, or adds a Microsoft advisory feed, this requirement SHALL be revisited rather than carried forward unexamined.

The record SHALL name what governs the Windows image's CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image digest pinned in `windows.Dockerfile`, and the cadence at which that pin is bumped.

The experience context is the maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` absent from the code-scanning dashboard. They find a stated reason and a pointer to the control that does apply, instead of re-opening an investigation that has already been done. Before this requirement the omission was indistinguishable from an oversight, and was filed as a bug.

#### Scenario: The exclusion is stated, not implied by absence

- **GIVEN** a maintainer reads the job that records images in Docker Scout
- **WHEN** they ask why `flutter-windows` is not among its legs
- **THEN** they find the exclusion recorded as a decision, with its reason
- **AND** the reason cites Scout's platform and size limits and its advisory coverage, not the release topology
- **AND** each cited fact carries the source that establishes it

#### Scenario: A disqualifier ceasing to hold reopens the decision

- **GIVEN** Docker Scout adds support for `windows/amd64` images
- **WHEN** a maintainer next reviews this requirement
- **THEN** the exclusion is re-examined against the remaining facts
- **AND** it is not carried forward on the strength of the superseded one

#### Scenario: Scout exclusion does not affect the other post-publish steps

- **GIVEN** `flutter-windows` is out of scope for Docker Scout
- **WHEN** a release publishes it
- **THEN** its anonymous-pull verification is unaffected, as `ci-image-anonymous-availability` specifies
- **AND** the exclusion is scoped to Scout recording alone

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only

The `release.yml` workflow SHALL continue to declare `workflow_dispatch:`. On `workflow_dispatch`, only the `release-windows` caller job SHALL execute; the Linux release job and the post-publish jobs (`update-description`, `record-image`, `create-github-release`) SHALL be skipped. The `FLUTTER_VERSION` env var SHALL be set from `github.ref_name`, so that a maintainer can rebuild a single tag's Windows image — through the same `windows-image.yml` reusable workflow — without re-cutting the Git tag and without re-publishing the Linux images, re-pushing the Docker Hub readme, or re-attempting `gh release create`.

Skipping SHALL be expressed as an explicit event guard on each job that must not run, not inferred from a `needs:` edge. A dependent job that declares `if: ... && !cancelled()` does not auto-skip when its dependency is skipped, so a `needs:` edge alone does not produce this behaviour.

The experience context is the maintainer recovering from a transient Windows runner failure: they re-run the workflow on the existing tag instead of force-pushing a new one. Linux recovery, by contrast, is the established fix-forward + re-tag pattern and does not need a `workflow_dispatch` path.

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild produces a fresh Windows image

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists in the repository
- **AND** the prior `release-windows` run for that tag failed
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the `release-windows` caller builds and pushes `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` to all three registries via `windows-image.yml`
- **AND** the existing Windows image digests at those tags are overwritten by the new digests

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild leaves the Linux digests untouched

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists and was previously published with Android digest `D_a`
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the Linux release job is reported as `skipped`
- **AND** `update-description`, `record-image`, and `create-github-release` are reported as `skipped`
- **AND** each of those jobs is skipped by its own event guard, not by a `needs:` edge to a skipped job
- **AND** the digest at `docker.io/<org>/flutter-android:X.Y.Z` remains `D_a`
- **AND** the run is reported as success (no failed jobs)

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The Windows image is out of scope for Docker Scout

`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, and the exclusion SHALL be justified by Scout's analysis support rather than by which job builds the image. The exclusion and its justification SHALL be discoverable by a maintainer reading the job that records images in Scout.

Three independent grounds each make the analysis impossible, and all three SHALL be recorded, each with the source that establishes it and the measurement that produced it, so a maintainer can re-derive them without consulting this change: the image's platform against Scout's supported architectures; the image's compressed size against Scout's analysis size limit; and Scout's advisory coverage against how the image's tools are installed.

The exclusion SHALL hold only while all three grounds hold. If any ceases to be true, this requirement SHALL be revisited rather than carried forward unexamined.

The record SHALL name what governs the Windows image's CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image digest pinned in `windows.Dockerfile`, and the cadence at which that pin is bumped.

The experience context is the maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` absent from the code-scanning dashboard. They find a stated reason and a pointer to the control that does apply, instead of re-opening an investigation that has already been done. Before this requirement the omission was indistinguishable from an oversight, and was filed as a bug.

#### Scenario: The exclusion is stated, not implied by absence

- **GIVEN** a maintainer reads the job that records images in Docker Scout
- **WHEN** they ask why `flutter-windows` is not among its legs
- **THEN** they find the exclusion recorded as a decision, with its reason
- **AND** the reason cites Scout's platform and size limits and its advisory coverage, not the release topology
- **AND** each cited fact carries the source that establishes it

#### Scenario: A disqualifier ceasing to hold reopens the decision

- **GIVEN** Docker Scout adds support for `windows/amd64` images
- **WHEN** a maintainer next reviews this requirement
- **THEN** the exclusion is re-examined against the remaining facts
- **AND** it is not carried forward on the strength of the superseded one

#### Scenario: Scout exclusion does not affect the other post-publish steps

- **GIVEN** `flutter-windows` is out of scope for Docker Scout
- **WHEN** a release publishes it
- **THEN** its anonymous-pull verification is unaffected, as `ci-image-anonymous-availability` specifies
- **AND** the exclusion is scoped to Scout recording alone

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only

The `release.yml` workflow SHALL continue to declare `workflow_dispatch:`. On `workflow_dispatch`, only the `release-windows` caller job SHALL execute; the Linux release job and the post-publish jobs (`update-description`, `record-image`, `create-github-release`) SHALL be skipped. The `FLUTTER_VERSION` env var SHALL be set from `github.ref_name`, so that a maintainer can rebuild a single tag's Windows image — through the same `windows-image.yml` reusable workflow — without re-cutting the Git tag and without re-publishing the Linux images, re-pushing the Docker Hub readme, or re-attempting `gh release create`.

Skipping SHALL be expressed as an explicit event guard on each job that must not run, not inferred from a `needs:` edge. A dependent job that declares `if: ... && !cancelled()` does not auto-skip when its dependency is skipped, so a `needs:` edge alone does not produce this behaviour.

The experience context is the maintainer recovering from a transient Windows runner failure: they re-run the workflow on the existing tag instead of force-pushing a new one. Linux recovery, by contrast, is the established fix-forward + re-tag pattern and does not need a `workflow_dispatch` path.

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild produces a fresh Windows image

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists in the repository
- **AND** the prior `release-windows` run for that tag failed
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the `release-windows` caller builds and pushes `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` to all three registries via `windows-image.yml`
- **AND** the existing Windows image digests at those tags are overwritten by the new digests

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild leaves the Linux digests untouched

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists and was previously published with Android digest `D_a`

## Why

`flutter-windows` has never been analyzed by Docker Scout. The `record-image`
job's matrix (`release.yml:236-238`) lists `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`
only, so no Scout environment record or CVE SARIF is produced for the Windows
image and it is absent from the code-scanning dashboard ([#506]).

[#506] asks to verify whether Scout produces meaningful output for a Windows
image before wiring it up. It does not, on three independent grounds — each
one disqualifying on its own:

1. **Architecture.** Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only
   ([docs](https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/)). The published image
   is `os: windows, arch: amd64`, read from its registry config blob rather
   than inferred. Not fixable: Windows containers are `windows/amd64` by
   construction.
2. **Size.** The same limit is 4 GB compressed. The published image is
   **5.90 GB across 37 layers**, the `servercore` base alone being 1.42 GB.
3. **No advisory data, and no inventory to apply it to.** Scout's 23 advisory
   sources include no Microsoft/MSRC feed, and every OS ecosystem it supports
   is a Linux one
   ([sources](https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/)).
   Nor would another scanner help: `windows.Dockerfile` installs Git from a zip
   (`:20`), Flutter via `git clone` (`:42`), and VS Build Tools via an
   installer (`:74`). None is registered with a package manager, so an
   SBOM-driven scanner finds an empty inventory. Trivy's supported-OS table has
   no Windows row; Grype delegates cataloguing to Syft, which has no MSI or KB
   cataloger.

So the current behaviour is right and the omission is not a bug. What is wrong
is that nothing says so: the exclusion reads as an oversight, and the spec that
does mention it justifies it by the wrong thing (see below).

Relevance gate: this changes what a maintainer finds when they notice
`flutter-windows` missing from the code-scanning dashboard — a recorded
decision and a pointer to what does govern its CVE posture, instead of a gap
that invites the same investigation again.

## What Changes

- A new requirement in `windows-image-release` stating that `flutter-windows`
  is out of scope for Docker Scout, carrying all three disqualifiers with the
  source for each, making the exclusion conditional on those facts continuing
  to hold, and naming what governs its CVE posture instead: the `servercore`
  base-image digest pin (`windows.Dockerfile:3`) and the cadence at which it is
  bumped. Microsoft rebuilds Windows base images monthly on Patch Tuesday —
  but that is upstream's cadence, not this repo's. Nothing here automates the
  bump: `.github/renovate.json`'s only Dockerfile manager reads Debian apt pins
  (`:58-59`), and no rule matches a `mcr.microsoft.com` image. That gap is real
  and is filed rather than fixed here (task 4.2).
- The existing *Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only* requirement
  is corrected. It currently justifies `record-image` skipping via
  `needs: release-android` (`spec.md:65`) — wrong twice over: no job named
  `release-android` exists (the code says `release-linux`, `release.yml:22`),
  and the skip is not produced by a `needs:` edge at all. Each downstream job
  carries an explicit `if: github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled()` guard
  (`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284`), and under `!cancelled()` a skipped
  dependency does **not** auto-skip its dependents. The spec describes a
  mechanism the code does not use.
- A comment at `record-image`'s matrix recording the exclusion and its reason,
  so the omission is legible where someone would notice it.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Adding a Windows-capable scanner. Researched and rejected above.
- Any change to which images `record-image` actually records. Behaviour is
  unchanged; only its justification and legibility change.
- Declaring the published image set in a config file. That is a separate
  concern with its own defects to fix, and coupling it here is what made an
  earlier attempt at this change unreviewable.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `windows-image-release`: gains a requirement placing `flutter-windows` out of
  scope for Docker Scout on stated technical grounds; its
  `workflow_dispatch` requirement is corrected to describe the skip mechanism
  the code actually uses and to stop naming a job that does not exist.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a comment at `record-image`'s
matrix, `:236-238`); `openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md` on archive.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The Windows image is out of scope for Docker Scout

`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, and the exclusion SHALL be justified by Scout's analysis support rather than by which job builds the image. The exclusion and its justification SHALL be discoverable by a maintainer reading the job that records images in Scout.

Three independent grounds each make the analysis impossible, and all three SHALL be recorded, each with the source that establishes it and the measurement that produced it, so a maintainer can re-derive them without consulting this change: the image's platform against Scout's supported architectures; the image's compressed size against Scout's analysis size limit; and Scout's advisory coverage against how the image's tools are installed.

The exclusion SHALL hold only while all three grounds hold. If any ceases to be true, this requirement SHALL be revisited rather than carried forward unexamined.

The record SHALL name what governs the Windows image's CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image digest pinned in `windows.Dockerfile`, and the cadence at which that pin is bumped.

The experience context is the maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` absent from the code-scanning dashboard. They find a stated reason and a pointer to the control that does apply, instead of re-opening an investigation that has already been done. Before this requirement the omission was indistinguishable from an oversight, and was filed as a bug.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only

The `release.yml` workflow SHALL continue to declare `workflow_dispatch:`. On `workflow_dispatch`, only the `release-windows` caller job SHALL execute; the Linux release job and the post-publish jobs (`update-description`, `record-image`, `create-github-release`) SHALL be skipped. The `FLUTTER_VERSION` env var SHALL be set from `github.ref_name`, so that a maintainer can rebuild a single tag's Windows image — through the same `windows-image.yml` reusable workflow — without re-cutting the Git tag and without re-publishing the Linux images, re-pushing the Docker Hub readme, or re-attempting `gh release create`.

Skipping SHALL be expressed as an explicit event guard on each job that must not run, not inferred from a `needs:` edge. A dependent job that declares `if: ... && !cancelled()` does not auto-skip when its dependency is skipped, so a `needs:` edge alone does not produce this behaviour.

The experience context is the maintainer recovering from a transient Windows runner failure: they re-run the workflow on the existing tag instead of force-pushing a new one. Linux recovery, by contrast, is the established fix-forward + re-tag pattern and does not need a `workflow_dispatch` path.

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild produces a fresh Windows image

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists in the repository
- **AND** the prior `release-windows` run for that tag failed
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the `release-windows` caller builds and pushes `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` to all three registries via `windows-image.yml`
- **AND** the existing Windows image digests at those tags are overwritten by the new digests

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild leaves the Linux digests untouched

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists and was previously published with Android digest `D_a`
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the Linux release job is reported as `skipped`
- **AND** `update-description`, `record-image`, and `create-github-release` are reported as `skipped`
- **AND** each of those jobs is skipped by its own event guard, not by a `needs:` edge to a skipped job
- **AND** the digest at `docker.io/<org>/flutter-android:X.Y.Z` remains `D_a`
- **AND** the run is reported as success (no failed jobs)

## Why

PR builds push a `pr-<N>` handoff tag for **both** Linux images:
`build.yml`'s matrix covers `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` (`:48-55`), and
the GHCR ref is built from `matrix.name` (`:64`, `:132-138`). Cleanup deletes
one of them. `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26` hardcodes
`PACKAGE_NAME: flutter-android`, and that single name is what the two API calls
query (`:66`, `:82`).

So every closed PR leaves a `flutter-web:pr-<N>` tag behind. Counted against
GHCR on 2026-08-10:

| Package | Handoff tags present |
|---|---|
| `flutter-android` | 2 — both open PRs, expected |
| `flutter-web` | **22** — `pr-513` through `pr-543` |

Each orphan is a full image index carrying SBOM and provenance attestations
(`build.yml:151-155`), not a bare tag. The count grows by one per PR.

The spec has the same defect: `ci-image-tag-lifecycle`'s Purpose and both
deletion requirements are scoped to `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android`
(`spec.md:5,11,17,43`). The workflow matches its spec — the spec was written
when `flutter-android` was the only image and never revisited when
`flutter-web` was added.

Relevance gate: this changes what a maintainer finds when auditing GHCR
storage — one tag per open PR, as the capability already promises, rather than
one per ever-opened PR on an image nobody was cleaning.

## What Changes

- `cleanup-pr-image.yml` iterates the images that produce handoff tags instead
  of naming one, with `fail-fast: false` so one image's failure does not skip
  another's.
- The 22 existing `flutter-web` orphans are swept once. The workflow fires only
  on `pull_request: closed` and `delete`, so it will never revisit tags for
  PRs that are already closed.
- `ci-image-tag-lifecycle` is de-scoped from `flutter-android` — its Purpose
  and its two deletion requirements.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Declaring the published image set in a config file. The image list here is
  short, local, and about which images produce *handoff tags* — a narrower
  question than which images are published. If a declaration lands later this
  workflow is a natural consumer, but it is not a prerequisite.
- `flutter-windows`, which produces no handoff tags: `windows.yml` calls
  `windows-image.yml` with `push: false` (`windows.yml:19-22`), so a PR
  builds it without pushing anything to delete.
- The two image-agnostic requirements in the capability, *Cleanup never
  targets a non-handoff tag* (`spec.md:47`) and *Cleanup workflow runs with
  minimum privilege* (`:68`). Both already hold for any image.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `ci-image-tag-lifecycle`: its two deletion requirements are de-scoped from
  `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android` to every image that produces handoff tags,
  and gain the guarantee that one image's cleanup failure does not skip
  another's.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/cleanup-pr-image.yml` (matrix over the image
names, `fail-fast: false`); `openspec/specs/ci-image-tag-lifecycle/spec.md` on
archive, including its Purpose line (`:5`).

**One-off**: sweep the orphaned `flutter-web` handoff tags. Deletion must
resolve a specific `pr-<N>` tag to a version ID and delete by ID — a
`tags == []` filter would match OCI index children and break parent tags.

**Verification**: after the sweep, each package should carry handoff tags only
for open PRs. The next closed PR should leave neither image with a `pr-<N>`
tag.

**Risk**: the sweep is a destructive registry operation. It is bounded by the
existing tag-regex guard (`:49-52`), which refuses anything that is not
`pr-<N>` or `branch-<ref>`, keeping release tags and `buildcache` unreachable —
but the one-off sweep runs outside that workflow, so it needs the same guard
applied deliberately rather than inherited.

On archive, the capability's Purpose (`openspec/specs/ci-image-tag-lifecycle/spec.md:5`) must lose its `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android` scoping — it is the prose form of this defect. The two requirements not restated below, *Cleanup never targets a non-handoff tag* (`:47`) and *Cleanup workflow runs with minimum privilege* (`:68`), are image-agnostic already and are deliberately unmodified.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: PR-close deletes the corresponding handoff tag

When a `pull_request` closes (merged or not), a workflow SHALL delete the GHCR tag `pr-<N>` corresponding to that PR number, on every image that produces handoff tags, if it exists.

Cleanup SHALL be independent per image: one image's deletion failing SHALL NOT prevent another's from being attempted.

The experience context is the maintainer auditing GHCR storage — they expect to see one tag per open PR, not per ever-opened PR, and not one image cleaned while another accumulates. Scoping cleanup to a single image is what let `flutter-web` reach 22 orphaned handoff tags while `flutter-android` stayed clean.

#### Scenario: Closing a merged PR removes the handoff tag from every image

- **GIVEN** PR #42 was opened on a same-repo branch, ran `build.yml`, and produced `pr-42` on both `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`
- **WHEN** PR #42 is merged
- **THEN** the cleanup workflow deletes `pr-42` from every image that produced it
- **AND** no image retains `pr-42` because cleanup did not name it

#### Scenario: Closing an unmerged PR removes the handoff tag

- **GIVEN** PR #42 produced `pr-42` and is closed without merging
- **WHEN** the cleanup workflow runs
- **THEN** `pr-42` is deleted from every image that produced it

#### Scenario: Cleanup is idempotent when the tag does not exist

- **GIVEN** PR #42 is from a fork (the artifact path was used; no GHCR tag was created)
- **WHEN** PR #42 closes and the cleanup workflow runs
- **THEN** each leg logs "tag not found, nothing to delete"
- **AND** the workflow exits 0 (does not fail)

#### Scenario: One image's cleanup failure does not skip another's

- **GIVEN** cleanup runs for several images and one image's deletion fails
- **WHEN** the workflow completes
- **THEN** the remaining images' handoff tags have still been deleted
- **AND** only the failing leg is reported red

### Requirement: Branch deletion deletes the corresponding branch handoff tag

When a branch is deleted (`delete` event with `ref_type == 'branch'`), the cleanup workflow SHALL delete the GHCR tag `branch-<branch-name>` (with `/` → `-`) if it exists, on every image that produces handoff tags.

The experience context is the maintainer running `workflow_dispatch` on a feature branch, then deleting the branch — they expect the `branch-<name>` tag to disappear automatically, from every image that built it, not only from the one the workflow happens to name.

#### Scenario: Branch deletion removes the branch handoff tag from every image

- **GIVEN** branch `feature/new-cache` was tested via `workflow_dispatch`, producing `branch-feature-new-cache` on every image that produces handoff tags
- **WHEN** the branch is deleted
- **THEN** the cleanup workflow computes `branch-feature-new-cache` from the deleted ref and deletes it from each image

content.text:
## First: the Renovate correction

PR #542 refutes my claim. Renovate **does** bump the `servercore` digest — weekly, with automerge, four times in history (#542, #435, #428, #425). My grep looked for an explicit `mcr.microsoft.com` rule, but none is needed: `config:recommended` enables the built-in `dockerfile` manager, and `renovate.json` disables only `github-actions`. I inferred absence of a rule meant absence of coverage.

Updated: the requirement now names Renovate as the live control, the proposal cites the evidence, and task 4.2 dropped that half — it's now only the stale `release-android` name in `ci-image-anonymous-availability`. Worktree also synced to `ae870a0`, and all three changes re-anchored (citations verified unchanged).

## Review result: APPROVED_WITH_WARNINGS — `pr-tag-cleanup-all-images`

**Criteria source:** all three loaded. Marker written.

**Zero CRITICALs.** All citations verified at `ae870a0`. Two things the reviewer checked harder than I did:

- **The `flutter-windows` exclusion is right** — verified past my citation: `windows-image.yml:154-155` gates the push on `inputs.push`, and the metadata action emits only the version tag. GHCR confirms zero `pr-*` tags on that package.
- **Delete-by-version-ID is genuinely necessary** — `flutter-web` has ~90 untagged versions (index children, attestations) alongside ~90 tagged. A `tags == []` filter would sweep them. Also confirmed no version carries more than one tag, so resolving a `pr-N` tag can't collaterally hit a release tag.

**W1 was a real error of mine, not staleness.** I claimed `flutter-android` "stayed clean." It hasn't:

| Package | Handoff tags | Orphans |
|---|---|---|
| `flutter-android` | 4 | **3** — `pr-454/455/456` |
| `flutter-web` | 33 | **32** — `pr-489`…`pr-543` |

Only #533 is open. So the android image *is* covered by the workflow and still has residue — a second, smaller defect with a different cause. My sweep was scoped to `flutter-web` only and would have left them, making task 2.7's own check fail. Both the proposal and the spec's experience context repeated the false premise; both fixed, and the sweep now covers both packages.

Also applied: **W2** removed the misplaced preamble (duplicated `tasks.md:3.1`), **W3** added a concrete open-PR re-check before DELETEs — a PR opening mid-sweep would otherwise have its tag deleted under a running build — and **W4/S1/S3** as smaller edits.

Two threads filed rather than fixed: `ci-image-handoff` hardcodes `flutter-android` while `web-image-testing:52` asserts `flutter-web:pr-<N>` exists — those two main specs contradict each other today, independent of this work.

`windows-description-sync` is the last one unreviewed.

All citations verified against `ae870a0`. Everything the artifacts cite checks out. Let me confirm one last point about the `!cancelled()` guard interaction, which bears on Risk-section soundness.

The proposal's Risk claim says on a Windows-only `workflow_dispatch` the job "is skipped by its own event guard (`:181`)" — verified: `if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled() }}` at line 181 does exactly that.

### CRITICAL issues

- `release.yml:178` — `needs: release-linux` ✓
- `:181` — `if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled() }}` ✓
- `:183` — `fail-fast: false` ✓

- `windows-image-release/spec.md:49` — the metadata-conventions requirement heading ✓
- `web-image-release/spec.md:57` — contains verbatim "The Docker Hub repository description for `flutter-web` SHALL be synced from `readme.md` on release, as the Android image is." ✓
- `release.yml:149-153` — `verify-published`'s matrix does list all three images ✓

The MODIFIED requirement restates `spec.md:49-61` faithfully. Machine diff shows exactly three deltas, all additive: one new paragraph, one clause appended to the experience-context sentence, one new scenario. The `docker/metadata-action` paragraph and the `Labels match Android conventions` scenario are byte-identical. Nothing dropped.

Sibling disjointness confirmed: `windows-scout-scope` MODIFIES *Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only* (`spec.md:65`) and ADDs a Scout requirement; this change MODIFIES *metadata conventions* (`:49`). Different requirements, different `release.yml` matrices (`:236-238` vs `:185-187`). `windows-scout-scope/tasks.md` already carries the coordination note: "Whichever archives second rebases its spec edit." Both can archive without clobbering.

Risk-section reasoning (question 4) is sound. `update-description` cannot sync a description before the image exists in any way that matters: `peter-evans/dockerhub-description` writes repo-level metadata via the Docker Hub API, not tag metadata, so ordering against `release-windows` is not a correctness constraint. The proposal itself flags the assumption as "unconfirmed" (`proposal.md:64`) — so the plan's own stated prerequisite has no completion criterion and no fallback branch. Note the push at `windows-image.yml` creates the repo implicitly on first push under most Docker Hub configurations, which would make 1.1 self-answering, but the artifacts never say so. Task 1.2 is the sharper risk: `DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN` scoped for push may lack repo-edit rights, and that failure mode is unaddressed beyond `fail-fast: false`.

2. **Docker Hub description sync is arguably not a "metadata convention"** (question 2). The requirement title is *Windows release uses the same metadata conventions as Android release*, and its body is entirely about `docker/metadata-action`, OCI labels, and `docker inspect`. The added paragraph is about a *registry web page*, synced by a different action (`peter-evans/dockerhub-description`) in a different job, on a different trigger path, with a different failure mode. The delta papers over this by widening the experience-context sentence to cover two distinct observers ("the operator inspecting `docker inspect`… — and the CI engineer opening the image's Docker Hub page"). The precedent argument is real — `web-image-release/spec.md:57` does exactly this — so this is consistency with an existing (questionable) shape rather than a new sin. A separate requirement would be more honest and would keep the two observers separable. This brushes `WARNING: Scope too broad — multiple unrelated experience contexts`.

3. **Task 3.2 is a verification with no stated method or artifact** (`tasks.md:17`): "Confirm no other capability claims ownership of Windows description sync, so the requirement lands in exactly one place." I ran this check — no other spec claims it; `generated-docs-and-examples/spec.md:7` says only that `readme.md` "SHALL be the file used both as the GitHub repository README and as the Docker Hub repository description", which is about *which file*, not *which images sync it*. So no delta is needed there and there is no duplication. But the task as written gives the implementer no way to know it is done.

4. **Task 2.2 is vague** (`tasks.md:11`): "Confirm the job's existing per-leg env … and its manifest read resolve correctly for the new leg". `IMAGE_REPOSITORY_PATH` is composed in `script/setEnvironmentVariables.js` as `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}/${IMAGE_REPOSITORY_NAME}` and is image-name-agnostic, so this resolves trivially. But "resolve correctly" names no expected value. It should state the expected output (`<owner>/flutter-windows`).

### Suggestions

1. Tasks 4.1–4.3 (`tasks.md:21-23`) are all post-merge observations gated on the next tag push — they cannot gate the PR. `windows-scout-scope/tasks.md` handles this explicitly ("This resolves only on a tag push, so it is a post-merge observation, not a merge gate"). Adopt the same annotation here so the change is not blocked on an unreachable checkbox at archive time.

2. The `windows-image.yml:95-97` citation supports "the metadata action names Docker Hub", not "the release path pushes there". The stronger citation for the actual push is the build/push step later in that workflow. Worth re-anchoring since it is the sole evidence for the prerequisite.

3. Consider whether the second added sentence — "Being published by a different job SHALL NOT be a reason for the Windows image's registry presentation to differ" — is a requirement or a rationale. It is unfalsifiable as a SHALL NOT (no observable outcome distinguishes compliance from violation beyond the first sentence). It reads as commentary and would sit better as prose in the experience context.

4. `windows-image-release/spec.md:65` still says `release-android` and misdescribes the skip mechanism as `needs:`-driven. This change touches the same file but correctly leaves that to `windows-scout-scope` (which fixes it at its task 2.1-2.3). No action needed — noting it so the archive-order rebase is not mistaken for a conflict.

### Verdict (one sentence)

All citations verify against `ae870a0`, the MODIFIED requirement restates the original faithfully with only additive changes, and the change is genuinely disjoint from both siblings — but the prerequisite tasks (1.1, 1.2) cannot be completed from the repo and carry no fallback, and bolting description sync onto a requirement titled "metadata conventions" mixes two experience contexts.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Windows release uses the same metadata conventions as Android release

The Windows release build SHALL use `docker/metadata-action` with the `images` input set to the same three registry namespaces and the `tags` input set to `type=raw,value=${{ env.FLUTTER_VERSION }}`, mirroring the Android job. This metadata step runs inside the reusable `windows-image.yml` workflow invoked by the `release-windows` caller. The image labels (`org.opencontainers.image.*`) produced by `metadata-action` SHALL be applied to the built image (as `--label` arguments to `docker build`), so that `docker inspect` reports the same OCI label set as the Android image. `docker/build-push-action` is not a viable mechanism here because it does not support Windows containers (tracked at https://github.com/docker/build-push-action/issues/18).

The Docker Hub repository description for `flutter-windows` SHALL be synced from `readme.md` on release, as the Android and web images are. Being published by a different job SHALL NOT be a reason for the Windows image's registry presentation to differ.

The experience context is the operator inspecting `docker inspect <org>/flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` and `docker inspect <org>/flutter-android:X.Y.Z` and finding the same set of OCI labels (description, source, revision, version) populated with the same values — and the CI engineer opening the image's Docker Hub page and finding the project readme rather than an empty description, as they would for either other image.

#### Scenario: Labels match Android conventions

- **GIVEN** a successful `release-windows` run for tag `X.Y.Z`
- **WHEN** an operator runs `docker inspect docker.io/<org>/flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` and inspects the `Labels` map
- **THEN** the keys `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `org.opencontainers.image.revision`, `org.opencontainers.image.version`, and `org.opencontainers.image.title` are all present
- **AND** `org.opencontainers.image.version` equals `X.Y.Z`
- **AND** `org.opencontainers.image.revision` equals the commit SHA of the tag

#### Scenario: The Docker Hub page carries the project readme

- **GIVEN** a tag push has published `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z`
- **WHEN** a CI engineer opens the `flutter-windows` repository page on Docker Hub
- **THEN** its description is the content of `readme.md`
- **AND** it matches what the `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` pages show

- **THEN** every published image's Docker Hub description is updated
- **AND** none is omitted for being produced by a different release job

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The Windows image's Docker Hub page carries the project readme

The Docker Hub repository description for `flutter-windows` SHALL be synced from `readme.md` on release, as the Android and web images are.

This is deliberately a separate requirement from the image's OCI metadata conventions. The two are observed differently — one through `docker inspect`, the other by opening a web page — produced by different actions in different jobs, and they fail in different ways. `web-image-release/spec.md:57` states the same guarantee for `flutter-web` inside its metadata requirement; that shape is not followed here, because folding a registry-page guarantee into a labels requirement obscures which one broke when a release goes wrong.

The experience context is the CI engineer who opens `hub.docker.com/r/<org>/flutter-windows` after finding the image in the readme's registry table. They see the project readme, as they would for either other image, rather than an empty page — the Windows image being built by a different job on a different runner is not something a reader of a registry page should be able to detect.

#### Scenario: The Docker Hub page carries the project readme

- **GIVEN** a tag push has published `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z`
- **WHEN** a CI engineer opens the `flutter-windows` repository page on Docker Hub
- **THEN** its description is the content of `readme.md`
- **AND** it matches what the `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` pages show

#### Scenario: Description sync covers every published image

- **GIVEN** a release publishes `flutter-android`, `flutter-web`, and `flutter-windows`
- **WHEN** the description-sync step runs
- **THEN** every published image's Docker Hub description is updated
- **AND** none is omitted for being produced by a different release job

1. `proposal.md:86-93` flags a real asymmetry — `update-description` declares `needs: release-linux` (`release.yml:178`) while the image it would newly describe is published by `release-windows` — and correctly notes the job's own event guard (`:181`) makes this moot on `workflow_dispatch`. 2. Task 3.2 (`tasks.md:17`) predicts the grep will find only `generated-docs-and-examples/spec.md:7`. I ran it: correct. `repository-wiki/spec.md:7` mentions Docker Hub but only as a place the README badge is seen; no delta needed there either. The prediction holds — consider recording that both were checked.

3. `windows-image-release/spec.md:65` (main, no delta here) still says the downstream jobs "auto-skip via their existing `needs: release-android`" and names a job that does not exist. `windows-scout-scope` fixes exactly this. If that change archives second it rebases cleanly, but if this one archives first the main spec will briefly carry a new correct requirement next to the stale one — call the ordering out in the PR rather than leaving it implicit.

### Verdict (one sentence)
Citations are sound and the two `windows-image-release` deltas are genuinely disjoint, but the ADDED requirement carries spec-structure rationale and an all-images scenario that both belong outside this capability, and task 1.2's token remedy needs to name the rotation it actually requires.

   - Delta headers: `## ADDED Requirements` / `## MODIFIED Requirements` / `## REMOVED Requirements`; MODIFIED must completely restate the requirement it replaces
   - `openspec validate <change> --strict`; requirement bodies must contain SHALL/MUST in the body's first line (not the header)
   - GitHub Actions: `!cancelled()` suppresses the implicit `success()` status check, so a job whose `needs:` dependency is *skipped* does NOT auto-skip
   - Docker Scout limits: `linux/amd64`/`linux/arm64` only; 4 GB compressed N/A threshold; 23 advisory sources with no Microsoft/MSRC feed
   - SBOM-driven scanners (Scout, Trivy, Grype/Syft) need a package-manager database; Windows Server Core has none
   - GHCR package version API; OCI index children appear as untagged versions
   - Renovate: `config:recommended` enables the built-in `dockerfile` manager (reads `FROM ... @sha256:` pins); this repo disables only `github-actions`

One PR. No dependencies on other changes. Line citations are against `ae870a0`.

## 1. Confirm the prerequisite

- [ ] 1.1 Confirm the `flutter-windows` repository exists on Docker Hub — open `hub.docker.com/r/<owner>/flutter-windows`, or `GET /v2/repositories/<owner>/flutter-windows/` against the Docker Hub API. The release path pushes there (`windows-image.yml:154-162`) and Docker Hub creates a repository on first push, so expect it to exist; this is a check, not a discovery
- [ ] 1.2 Confirm `DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN` can edit repository descriptions, not only push — a push-scoped token cannot, and `peter-evans/dockerhub-description` fails on it. Check the token's scopes in Docker Hub account settings. Note the existing `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` legs already succeed with this token (`release.yml:218`), which is strong evidence the scope is sufficient; confirm rather than re-derive
- [ ] 1.3 If the scope is insufficient, note that Docker Hub token scopes are immutable: the remedy is to mint a new token with repo-write scope and rotate the `DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN` secret, which is consumed in 8 places (`release.yml:87,129,218,254`, `windows-image.yml:108`, `ci.yml:43`, `build.yml:102,307`). That is its own change — do not fold it in here, and do not add the leg until it lands, since `fail-fast: false` (`release.yml:183`) would leave a permanently red leg reporting a permissions problem as a release failure

## 2. Cover the Windows image

- [ ] 2.1 Add `flutter-windows` to `update-description`'s matrix (`release.yml:185-187`)
- [ ] 2.2 Confirm the new leg resolves `IMAGE_REPOSITORY_PATH` to `<owner>/flutter-windows`. It is composed in `script/setEnvironmentVariables.js` from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER` and `IMAGE_REPOSITORY_NAME` (`release.yml:189`), both image-agnostic, so this should hold — confirm the job log rather than assuming
- [ ] 2.3 Confirm `fail-fast: false` is already set so one image's sync failure does not skip the others — it is at `release.yml:183`

## 3. Close the spec gap

- [ ] 3.1 On archive, add the new description-sync requirement to `openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md` as its own requirement — not folded into *Windows release uses the same metadata conventions as Android release* (`:49`), which stays untouched
- [ ] 3.2 Confirm no other capability claims Windows description sync: grep `openspec/specs/` for `dockerhub-description` and `repository description`. Expect two hits, neither needing a delta: `generated-docs-and-examples/spec.md:7` governs *which file* is used (`readme.md`), not which images sync it; `repository-wiki/spec.md:7` mentions Docker Hub only as a place the README badge is seen

## 4. Verification

All three resolve only on the next tag push, so they are post-merge observations, not merge gates.

- [ ] 4.1 After the next release, confirm `hub.docker.com/r/<org>/flutter-windows` shows the project readme
- [ ] 4.2 Confirm the `flutter-windows` leg of `update-description` ran and succeeded — the observable behind scenario 1. The other two legs are unchanged by this work
- [ ] 4.3 Confirm the `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` descriptions are unchanged by the added leg

## 5. Wrap-up

- [ ] 5.1 Open the PR with a Conventional Commit title, one logical concern
- [ ] 5.2 Note in the PR that `record-image`'s omission of `flutter-windows` is deliberate and separate, handled by `windows-scout-scope`
- [ ] 5.3 Note the archive ordering: `windows-image-release/spec.md:65` still names `release-android` and misdescribes the dispatch-skip mechanism. `windows-scout-scope` fixes it. If this change archives first, the main spec briefly carries the new correct requirement beside that stale one — call it out rather than leaving it implicit

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The Windows image's Docker Hub page carries the project readme

The Docker Hub repository description for `flutter-windows` SHALL be synced from `readme.md` on release, as the Android and web images are. Being published by a different release job SHALL NOT leave the Windows image's registry page unsynced.

The experience context is the CI engineer who opens `hub.docker.com/r/<org>/flutter-windows` after finding the image in the readme's registry table. They see the project readme, as they would for either other image, rather than an empty page — the Windows image being built by a different job on a different runner is not something a reader of a registry page should be able to detect.

#### Scenario: The Docker Hub page carries the project readme

- **GIVEN** a tag push has published `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z`
- **WHEN** a CI engineer opens the `flutter-windows` repository page on Docker Hub
- **THEN** its description is the content of `readme.md`
- **AND** it matches what the `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` pages show

#### Scenario: A Linux release failure does not leave the Windows page unsynced

- **GIVEN** a tag push where `release-windows` publishes `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z`
- **WHEN** the description-sync step runs
- **THEN** the `flutter-windows` page is synced from `readme.md`
- **AND** it is not skipped on account of which job published the image

- [ ] 1.1 Add a comment at `record-image`'s matrix (`release.yml:236-238`) stating that `flutter-windows` is excluded, with all three reasons and the source for each: Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only while the image is `windows/amd64`; the 4 GB compressed limit against the image's 5.90 GB; and no Microsoft advisory feed, with the image's tools installed outside any package manager
- [ ] 1.2 Include the source for each ground, so the comment is re-verifiable without the proposal: <https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/> for the architecture and size limits, <https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/> for advisory coverage
- [ ] 1.3 Record how the image's own figures were measured, not just the figures: platform (`os`/`architecture`) from the published tag's registry config blob, and compressed size by summing layer sizes in its manifest. A future reader re-checking a 4 GB limit against a 5.90 GB image needs to know which number to re-measure
- [ ] 1.4 Name the control that does apply — the `servercore` digest pin at `windows.Dockerfile:3`, which Renovate bumps automatically (built-in `dockerfile` manager, weekly schedule, automerge; e.g. PR #542) — so the comment points at a live control rather than only saying "no"
- [ ] 1.5 Match the neighbouring comment at `release.yml:135-139` in form — prose sentences, no bullet list, wrapped at the file's existing width — since it is the repo's precedent for recording why a job is wired the way it is. - [ ] 3.2 Confirm no other spec asserts that `flutter-windows` is scanned or recorded. `ci-image-vulnerability-scan` covers the PR-time `scan_image` job (that spec's name for it; the workflow job is `scan-image`) and is scoped to `flutter-android` throughout — it never mentions `flutter-windows`, so it needs no delta
- [ ] 3.3 Re-check the three disqualifiers against Docker's current docs before merging — they are the whole basis of the requirement, and the requirement makes the exclusion conditional on them
- [ ] 3.4 After the next release, confirm `record-image` ran with the same two legs and the same SARIF categories as before. This resolves only on a tag push, so it is a post-merge observation, not a merge gate

## 1. Clean every image that produces handoff tags

- [ ] 1.5 Confirm the tag-regex guard (`:49-52`) is unchanged and still refuses anything that is not `pr-<N>` or `branch-<ref>`, so release tags and `buildcache` stay unreachable

- [ ] 2.1 Re-count handoff tags on **both** packages immediately before the sweep — 33 on `flutter-web` and 4 on `flutter-android` as of 2026-08-11, and both will have moved. Work from the fresh list, not the recorded one

- [ ] 2.3 Build the open-PR exclusion list from `gh api "/repos/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/pulls?state=open" --jq '[.[].number]'`, and re-check it immediately before issuing any DELETE — not only at 2.1. A PR opened mid-sweep would otherwise have its handoff tag deleted under a running build, breaking `test-image`'s pull (`build.yml:258`) and `scan-image`'s digest resolve (`:322`)
- [ ] 2.4 Apply the same regex guard the workflow uses (`^pr-[0-9]+$`, `^branch-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`) to every tag on the sweep list before deleting anything, since the one-off runs outside the workflow that enforces it
- [ ] 2.5 Delete by resolving each `pr-<N>` tag to a version ID and deleting that ID — **never** a `tags == []` filter, which matches OCI index children and would break parent tags
- [ ] 2.6 Dry-run first: print the resolved (tag, version_id) pairs and confirm the list against 2.1 before any DELETE is issued

## 3. De-scope the spec

- [ ] 3.1 On archive, drop the `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android` scoping from the capability Purpose (`openspec/specs/ci-image-tag-lifecycle/spec.md:5`)
- [ ] 3.2 Confirm the two requirements left unmodified — *Cleanup never targets a non-handoff tag* (`:47`) and *Cleanup workflow runs with minimum privilege* (`:68`) — still read correctly for a multi-image workflow, and that `permissions:` needs no change for the added legs

## 4. Verification

- [ ] 4.1 Close a PR after the change lands and confirm neither image retains its `pr-<N>` tag
- [ ] 4.2 Confirm the run shows exactly two legs (`flutter-android`, `flutter-web`), and that a leg with nothing to delete is green rather than red — asserting the count catches a future image that silently fails to appear
- [ ] 4.3 Confirm no release tag or `buildcache` tag was touched by either the workflow or the sweep

## 5. Wrap-up

- [ ] 5.1 Open the PR with a Conventional Commit title, one logical concern. The group-2 sweep is not part of the PR — it is a manual registry operation with no diff, tracked here and recorded in the PR body
- [ ] 5.2 Note in the PR the orphan count swept and that deletion resolved version IDs rather than filtering on empty tags
- [ ] 5.3 File an issue for the same defect one capability upstream: `ci-image-handoff/spec.md:13,15,26,27` hardcodes `flutter-android` in the outputs that *produce* the tags this change deletes, while `web-image-testing/spec.md:52` already asserts `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-web:pr-<N>` exists. The two main specs contradict each other today, independent of this change. Out of scope here — fixing it would break the one-logical-concern rule

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: PR-close deletes the corresponding handoff tag

When a `pull_request` closes (merged or not), a workflow SHALL delete the GHCR tag `pr-<N>` corresponding to that PR number, on every image that produces handoff tags, if it exists.

Cleanup SHALL be independent per image: one image's deletion failing SHALL NOT prevent another's from being attempted.

The experience context is the maintainer auditing GHCR storage — they expect to see one tag per open PR, not per ever-opened PR, and not one image cleaned while another accumulates. Scoping cleanup to a single image is what let `flutter-web` accumulate an orphaned handoff tag for every PR it ever built, while the image the workflow does name stayed within a few.

#### Scenario: Closing a merged PR removes the handoff tag from every image

- **GIVEN** PR #42 was opened on a same-repo branch, ran `build.yml`, and produced `pr-42` on both `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`
- **WHEN** PR #42 is merged
- **THEN** the cleanup workflow deletes `pr-42` from every image that produced it
- **AND** no image retains `pr-42` because cleanup did not name it

#### Scenario: Closing an unmerged PR removes the handoff tag

- **GIVEN** PR #42 produced `pr-42` and is closed without merging
- **WHEN** the cleanup workflow runs
- **THEN** `pr-42` is deleted from every image that produced it

#### Scenario: Cleanup is idempotent when the tag does not exist

- **GIVEN** PR #42 is from a fork (the artifact path was used; no GHCR tag was created)
- **WHEN** PR #42 closes and the cleanup workflow runs
- **THEN** each leg logs "tag not found, nothing to delete"
- **AND** the workflow exits 0 (does not fail)

#### Scenario: One image's cleanup failure does not skip another's

- **GIVEN** cleanup runs for several images and one image's deletion fails
- **WHEN** the workflow completes
- **THEN** the remaining images' handoff tags have still been deleted
- **AND** only the failing leg is reported red

### Requirement: Branch deletion deletes the corresponding branch handoff tag

When a branch is deleted (`delete` event with `ref_type == 'branch'`), the cleanup workflow SHALL delete the GHCR tag `branch-<branch-name>` (with `/` → `-`) if it exists, on every image that produces handoff tags.

The experience context is the maintainer running `workflow_dispatch` on a feature branch, then deleting the branch — they expect the `branch-<name>` tag to disappear automatically, from every image that built it, not only from the one the workflow happens to name.

#### Scenario: Branch deletion removes the branch handoff tag from every image

- **GIVEN** branch `feature/new-cache` was tested via `workflow_dispatch`, producing `branch-feature-new-cache` on every image that produces handoff tags
- **WHEN** the branch is deleted
- **THEN** the cleanup workflow computes `branch-feature-new-cache` from the deleted ref and deletes it from each image
